questions.question: __________are in Madhya Pradesh.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bagh caves.**__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bagh Caves** is situated among the southern slopes of the Vindhyas in Bagh town of Dhar district in **Madhya Pradesh state in central India.**
 
• The Bagh Caves are a group of nine rock-cut monuments, great examples of Indian rock-cut architecture.
 
• They are believed to been built during the 5th-7th century, carved during the Satvahana dynasty. The Archaeological Survey of India has restored the place for over 17 years.
 
• These caves belong to the Buddhist faith and it is not certain, how and when these caves began to be called Bagh Gupha.
 
• The most beautiful paintings known to be created by prehistoric man can be found in these rock-cut caverns. Only 5 of the original 9 caverns have survived.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Bhaja caves are a group o**f 22 rock-cut caves** located in the city of Pune, India. The caves are 400ft above the village of Bhaja. This cave belongs to the Early Buddhist schools in Maharashtra.
 
• **Kanheri caves** are a group of caves and rock-cut monuments, in the forests of The Sanjay Gandhi National Park, on the western outskirts of Mumbai, India. They contain Buddhist sculptures, carvings, paintings, and inscriptions.
 
• **Ajanta caves** are 30 rock-cut Buddhist cave monuments in the Aurangabad district of Maharashtra state in India. The caves include paintings and rock-cut sculptures described as among the finest examples of ancient Indian art, particularly expressive paintings that present emotions through gesture, pose, and form.

questions.question: The ceremonial gateway in a Stupa is also known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Torana**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• 
 
 The Indian gateway, usually of stone, marking the entrance to a Buddhist shrine or stupa or to a Hindu temple is known as "**Torana**".

 
 
• 
 
It is a free-standing ornamental or arched gateway for ceremonial purposes seen in the Hindu, Buddhist, and Jain architecture of the Indian subcontinent, Southeast Asia, and parts of East Asia.

 
 
• 
 
Toranas typically consist of **two pillars** carrying two or three transverse beams that extend beyond the pillars on either side.

 
 
• 
 
The **four toranas** of the **Great Stupa** at **Sanchi** are great examples.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Medhi** is a circular terrace or a **path** enclosed by a railing that surrounds the dome, on which the devotees circumambulate in the clockwise direction.
 
• A **vedika** is a wooden fence that surrounds a sacred place that can be free-standing at ground level.
 
• In Buddhism and Hinduism, the **Chhatra** is an auspicious symbol representing royalty and protection. It is in the form of a stone disk typically decorated at the apex of a Buddhist stupa.

questions.question: The rocky outer part of Earth is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**the lithosphere**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The rigid, rocky outer layer of the Earth is called the lithosphere, it consist of the crust and the solid outermost layer of the upper **mantle**.
 
• It depth of it is extended to **100km**.
 
• It comprises the rocks of the earth’s crust and the thin layers of soil that contain nutrient elements that **sustain organisms**.
 
• The earth’s surface has **2** main divisions.
 
• The large land masses are known as the **continents** and the huge water bodies are called the **ocean basins**.
 
• There are 2 types of the **lithosphere**, one is oceanic lithosphere and other one is continental lithosphere.
 
• The oceanic lithosphere is associated with the **oceanic crust**, and it is slightly denser than the continental lithosphere.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Earth's **outer** core is a fluid layer about 2,260 km thick, composed of mostly iron and nickel that lies above Earth's solid inner core and below its mantle.
 
• The **inner** core is the innermost layer of the Earth and is located at the direct center of the Earth below the outer core.
 
• The **mantle** lies between Earth's dense, super-heated core and its thin outer layer, the crust.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a method used for measuring unemployment in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Unusual Status Approach**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Methods used for measuring **unemployment** in India are the Weekly status Approach, Daily status Approach and **Usual Status Approach.**
 
• These measures enable the existing unemployment rate in the economy for quantification and hence helps in taking **remedial steps**.
 
• Based on time and willingness criteria unemployment mainly open unemployment and underemployment have been estimated using the following 3 approaches headed by **Prof. M L. Dantwala**.
 
• Various reasons leads to unemployment which can vary from **seasonal to technological advancements**, and hence requires diverse measures to estimate the presence of unemployment in the economy. 
 
• The** daily status approach **is an inclusive and accurate measure to estimate unemployment because it takes into account the informal workers such as those engaged in agriculture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Weekly status Approach measures unemployment with respect to one **week**. 
 
• In **Daily status Approach**, unemployment status of a person is measured for each day in a reference week.
 
• **Usual status approach** measures the number of persons who remained unemployed for a major part of the year and gives the lowest estimates of unemployment.

questions.question: Identify the group of insulators from the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __'**Plastic, wood and rubber**'.__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Insulators **are materials that do not have free electrons, therefore they do not conduct electricity.
 
• Some examples of insulators are Sulphur, Mika, and Polythene.
 
• **Plastic, wood, and rubber **don't have free electrons moving around so they can't conduct heat and electricity which gives them the property of good insulators.
 
• Most non-metal materials such as plastic, wood, and rubber are insulators.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Iron has metallic bonds which are where the electrons are free to move around more than one atom.
 
• This is called delocalization. Because of this,** iron is a good conductor.**

• In this festival villagers play drums and go to the mountains to collect flowers named **Larda**.
 
• This festival is celebrated in **remembrance** of the people who passed away.
 
• It is celebrated mainly in the **kinnaur** district of Himachal Pradesh
 
• This festival is celebrated on the **16th** day of the Hindu month of Bhadrapada.

questions.question: The State Policy Directive Principles are some of the ideas outlined in Articles 36 through ____________ of the Constitution of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**51**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The State Policy Directive Principles are some of the ideas outlined in **Articles 36** through **51** of the **Constitution of India.**** **
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy aim to create **social and economic** conditions.
 
• Through a **welfare** state, they aim to establish social and economic democracy.
 
• Though the Directive Principles are non-justiciable rights of the people but fundamental in the governance of the country, it shall be the duty of the State to apply these principles in making laws per** Article 37**.
 
• All executive agencies of unions and states should also be guided by these **directive principles**.
 
• Even the **judiciary** should keep them in mind for the decision in cases.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Constitution of India is the **supreme law** of India.
 
• The constitution of India was enacted on **26th of November,1949**.
 
• The constitution of India was drafted by **B.R. Ambedkar**.
